description: The srl toolchain: application scaffold, dev server, project model, template checker, and the production artifact build and release pipeline
author: Bernardo Giordano
//: THE TOOLCHAIN, AS A PACKAGE OF ITS OWN.
This directory is the package, the same way source/ is: a standalone checkout
would have cli/ at its root beside the library, and extracting it is a file
move. What is in here is every tool a repository built on srl needs and none
of the tools that only make sense inside this repository — those stay in
tools/ at the root and are published nowhere. cli/scaffold/ is the newest of
them, and the reason is the rule itself: the shape of a correct application
was a fixture in tools/, which is to say it was written down where no
Separate from @srljs/core rather than folded into it, for one reason: the
build needs Vite, parse5 and the TypeScript compiler API, and the consumer
this framework is actually for — a browser with an import map and no build
step — must not have to install a hundred megabytes of bundler to load a
library that never runs one. @srljs/core keeps its two runtime dependencies.
A page installs the library; a repository that deploys one installs this too.
The two are released together and pinned to each other, not to a range. This
package reads the library's own manifest for the mounts and specifier
prefixes (cli/package/interface.mjs), and imports three of its modules
outright, so the pair is one interface split across two tarballs.
//bin: One name, and a dispatcher behind it. Every tool is still a module runnable by
path — the bin adds a name rather than a layer, and cli/bin/srl.mjs parses
nothing a tool would parse for itself.
//files: The tool directories, minus the suite. cli/test/ tests this package rather
than being it, and its fixtures are whole projects a consumer has no use for.
README.md and LICENSE are not listed because npm ships them either way, and
source/package.json does not list them either.
No `exports` map. Every entry point here is a module path a script names, and

same file both already assume. Narrowing it would be a second description of
//peerDependencies: The library, exactly. cli/package/interface.mjs reads its manifest and three
of its modules are imported outright: the manifest policy the build admits
remotes against and the template dialect the checker refuses expressions with
are the same ones the runtime enforces. A range here would let a consumer pair

Not a `dependency`, because the consumer installs the library for its own
sake: it is what their application imports. A dependency here would give them
a second copy under this package the day their own pin drifted.
//dependencies: Pinned exactly, and to the versions this repository's own lockfile resolves,
because that is the point of publishing the toolchain rather than telling a
consumer to copy three pins into their package.json. tools/checks/verify-deps.mjs
fails when these and the root devDependencies drift apart.
vite        the bundler the build drives. Implementation, not interface:
callers get one function and one artifact report.
typescript  the compiler API, for the template checker's program and for
the build's own AST passes. The 6.x install, not tsgo: the
Go-native compiler ships no public API until 7.1.
parse5      spec HTML parsing, so a production index.html is a transform of
a parsed tree rather than a regular expression over markup.
Tailwind is deliberately absent. The build shells out to the consumer's own
`node_modules/.bin/tailwindcss` because the stylesheet it compiles is theirs,
written against their config and their version. A copy pinned here would
compile their CSS with a compiler they did not choose.
//devDependencies: The artifact suite drives a real Chrome over the DevTools protocol to load a
built page from a served origin, which is the only way to catch an artifact
that assembles cleanly and does not run. Nothing here ships.
